When we have learned a skill or a piece of information by practicing until we acquire complete mastery, we are�overlearning.

For example: You practiced playing scales on a piano over and over again. Even after you had already mastered the skill of playing scales, you still continued to practice. Eventually, you hit a plateau and didn't get any better or faster at playing scales but you kept practicing them for 20 minutes every day anyway. Then you went away on vacation for two weeks and didn't practice. When you got back, you were still able to play scales very well because you had already overlearned the skill.�

Without overlearning (if we only learn something to the point where we barely know it) rapid forgetting will occur because the information is not firmly anchored in memory. That s what happens when students  cram for an exam. You learn the material quickly, often the night or the hour before the test, then forget it soon after writing the exam.�

Another example:�you may have learned the lines for a play just in time for the performance, but a week later you cannot remember any of them because you did not overlearn the material.

Overlearning has its advantages and disadvantages. An advantage of overlearning is that the learner masters and�really�learns the material or skill. Once something is overlearned, the learner has gained full mastery of the topic and that understanding will persist over a long period of time. At a certain point, however, overlearning reaches a maximum when the learner can learn and understand the material without mistakes or hesitations. A disadvantage of overlearning is that once the learner knows the material thoroughly, any extra time spent reviewing this body of knowledge is time wasted.�The name for this situation is�diminishing returns.�Extra studying does not lead to extra gains in learning.

For example, if a high school math teacher decided to review the addition of whole numbers, that would involve overlearning because students would be bored with a presentation of information that is very familiar to them, that they have already mastered.
